title: A Better Way to Measure Obesity: Moving Beyond BMI
subtitle: New research suggests that the traditional body mass index may not be the best tool for diagnosing health risks.

summary.en: Doctors are looking for better ways to identify obesity beyond the traditional Body Mass Index (BMI). A new study shows that BMI often misdiagnoses millions of people worldwide. The proposed method uses waist measurements and organ function tests to get a clearer picture of health. Experts believe this approach will help doctors treat patients more accurately. While the new process is more complex, it could lead to better long-term health outcomes.
summary.zh: 醫師們正在尋求比傳統身體質量指數（BMI）更好的肥胖判定方式。一項新研究顯示，身體質量指數經常導致全球數百萬人被誤診。所提出的新方法採用腰圍測量與器官功能檢測，以獲得更清晰的健康圖像。專家認為，這種方法將有助於醫師更精確地治療病患。雖然新流程較為複雜，但它有望帶來更好的長期健康成果。

paragraphs.en: For many years, doctors have used the Body Mass Index (BMI) to decide if a person is overweight or obese. BMI is a simple calculation that divides a person's weight by their height. While it is easy to use, many medical experts now say it is a "blunt instrument"—a tool that is not precise enough for such a serious health diagnosis. According to The Guardian Health, this method may be causing millions of people to be misdiagnosed every year.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，醫師一直使用身體質量指數（BMI）來判定一個人是否過重或肥胖。身體質量指數是一種簡單的計算方式，將一個人的體重除以其身高的平方。雖然使用起來很方便，但許多醫學專家現在認為這是一個「粗糙的工具」，對於如此嚴肅的健康診斷而言，其精確度不足。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，這種方法每年可能導致數百萬人被誤診。

paragraphs.en: BMI is currently used by health organizations around the world to classify over a billion people. In the United States, more than 70% of adults are classified as overweight or obese based on this number alone. However, critics argue that BMI does not tell the whole story. It often misses people who have dangerous levels of body fat, while at the same time, it may incorrectly label healthy individuals as having a weight problem. Francisco Rubino, a professor at King’s College London, noted that this inaccuracy is a major problem for both individual patients and the global healthcare system.
paragraphs.zh: 目前全球各地的衛生組織都使用身體質量指數來對超過十億人進行分類。在美國，僅憑這個數字，就有超過百分之七十的成年人被歸類為過重或肥胖。然而，批評者認為身體質量指數並未呈現全貌。它經常遺漏那些體內脂肪含量已達危險程度的人，同時也可能錯誤地將健康的人標記為有體重問題。倫敦國王學院（King’s College London）教授法蘭西斯科·魯比諾（Francisco Rubino）指出，這種不準確性對個別病患和全球醫療體系而言都是一個重大問題。

paragraphs.en: To solve this, researchers have proposed a new way to diagnose obesity. This approach was recently detailed in a report by a group of world experts. Instead of relying only on height and weight, doctors would look at a combination of factors. This includes measuring a person's waist and checking how well their organs are working. By using these extra tests, doctors can better distinguish between a person who is healthy and a person who is at risk of serious illness.
paragraphs.zh: 為了改善這一點，研究人員提出了一種診斷肥胖的新方法。這項方法近期在一份由全球專家組成的報告中詳述。醫師不再僅依賴身高和體重，而是會綜合考量多項因素。這包括測量一個人的腰圍，並檢查其器官的運作狀況。透過這些額外的檢測，醫師能更有效地分辨出誰是健康的人，以及誰正處於罹患嚴重疾病的風險中。

paragraphs.en: Under this new system, the diagnosis is split into two categories. The first is "pre-clinical obesity," where a person has extra fat that could become a health risk in the future. The second is "clinical obesity," which describes a situation where excess fat is already causing damage to the body's organs. This is an important change because it helps doctors see the difference between someone who is simply carrying extra weight and someone who is actually sick. According to The Guardian Health, this method allows doctors to treat patients at the individual level rather than using a one-size-fits-all number.
paragraphs.zh: 在這一套新系統下，診斷被分為兩類。第一類是「臨床前期肥胖」，指一個人擁有過多的脂肪，未來可能成為健康風險；第二類是「臨床肥胖」，描述的是過多脂肪已經對身體器官造成損害的情況。這是一個重要的改變，因為它有助於醫師區分單純體重較重的人與真正生病的人。根據《衛報健康》報導，這種方法讓醫師能夠針對個別病患進行治療，而不是套用一個一體適用的數字。

paragraphs.en: One of the most interesting findings from the research is that many people with a high BMI are not actually "obese" under the new definition. In fact, some of these individuals have a lower risk of death than people who were previously considered healthy. The study, which looked at health records from over 800,000 people in countries including the UK, the US, China, and Spain, found that most people with pre-clinical obesity did not develop active disease over a ten-year period. This suggests that the old way of measuring health might have been causing unnecessary worry for many people.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究中最有趣的發現之一是，許多身體質量指數偏高的人，按照新的定義其實並不屬於「肥胖」。事實上，其中一些人的死亡風險甚至比先前被認為健康的人還要低。這項研究檢視了包括英國、美國、中國和西班牙在內，超過八十萬人的健康紀錄，發現大多數處於臨床前期肥胖的人，在十年內並未發展出活動性疾病。這顯示舊有的健康測量方式，可能讓許多人產生了不必要的擔憂。

paragraphs.en: Of course, there are challenges to changing how we diagnose obesity. The new method is more complex for doctors to perform. It requires more time and more tests than simply calculating a BMI score. However, supporters of the new approach argue that the benefits are worth the extra effort. By focusing on how fat affects the body's organs, doctors can provide better care and focus their attention on the patients who are truly at risk.
paragraphs.zh: 當然，改變肥胖的診斷方式也面臨挑戰。對醫師而言，新方法執行起來較為複雜。與單純計算身體質量指數相比，它需要花費更多時間並進行更多檢測。然而，新方法的支持者認為，這些努力所帶來的益處是值得的。透過關注脂肪如何影響身體器官，醫師可以提供更好的照護，並將注意力集中在真正處於風險中的病患身上。

paragraphs.en: As we look to the future, it is clear that the medical community is moving toward a more personalized approach to health. While BMI will likely remain a common tool because of its simplicity, it may no longer be the final word on a person's health status. By combining traditional measurements with modern tests, doctors hope to prevent millions of misdiagnoses and help people live healthier lives. This shift represents a significant step forward in our understanding of how weight and health are connected, moving away from simple numbers toward a deeper, more accurate picture of human well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，顯而易見的是，醫學界正朝向更個人化的健康照護方式邁進。雖然身體質量指數因其簡單易用，很可能會繼續作為常見的工具，但它可能不再是判定一個人健康狀況的最終標準。透過結合傳統測量與現代檢測，醫師希望能避免數百萬次的誤診，並幫助人們過上更健康的生活。這種轉變代表我們在理解體重與健康之間的關聯上，邁出了重要的一步，從單純的數字轉向對人類福祉更深入、更精確的描繪。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A tool or method that is not precise or subtle enough for a specific task.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 粗糙的工具；不夠精確的方法。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「鈍器」，這裡比喻方法不夠細緻。文中：While it is easy to use, many medical experts now say it is a "blunt instrument"—a tool that is not precise enough for such a serious health diagnosis.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To provide all the necessary facts or information about a situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 說明事情的全部真相；呈現完整狀況。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常用於否定句，表示資訊不完整。文中：However, critics argue that BMI does not tell the whole story.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Designed to be suitable for everyone, regardless of individual differences.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 一體適用的；不分情況統一處理的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 原指衣服尺寸，這裡形容醫療診斷方式過於籠統。文中：According to The Guardian Health, this method allows doctors to treat patients at the individual level rather than using a one-size-fits-all number.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The definitive or last opinion/decision on a matter.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指 BMI 不再是判斷健康的唯一標準。文中：While BMI will likely remain a common tool because of its simplicity, it may no longer be the final word on a person's health status.

quiz.question: According to the new diagnostic system proposed by researchers, what is the primary difference between 'pre-clinical obesity' and 'clinical obesity'?

options.A: Pre-clinical obesity is determined by height, while clinical obesity is determined by waist size.
options.B: Pre-clinical obesity involves extra fat that may become a risk, while clinical obesity involves fat that is already damaging organs.
options.C: Pre-clinical obesity refers to patients who have lost weight, while clinical obesity refers to those who have gained it.
options.D: Pre-clinical obesity requires immediate medical treatment, while clinical obesity does not require any intervention.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，文中明確定義『pre-clinical obesity』是指身上有額外脂肪但尚未造成傷害，而『clinical obesity』則是脂肪已經對器官造成損害。選項 A 錯誤，因為新系統並非僅依賴單一測量值；選項 C 與文章內容無關；選項 D 則完全顛倒了治療的優先順序。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might some people with a 'high BMI' actually have a lower risk of death than those considered 'healthy'?

options.A: Because they exercise more frequently than people with a lower BMI.
options.B: Because BMI is a perfect indicator of overall muscle mass and fitness.
options.C: Because their body fat is not currently causing damage to their organs.
options.D: Because they have already undergone medical treatments to lower their weight.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段與第三段的推論，BMI 高並不代表身體一定不健康，關鍵在於脂肪是否造成了器官損害。如果一個人的 BMI 高，但脂肪並未損害其器官（屬於 pre-clinical），其健康風險可能比被標籤為『健康』但實際上有隱性問題的人還低。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 B 與文章主旨衝突；選項 D 則為無根據的推測。

quiz.question: In the first paragraph, the author describes BMI as a 'blunt instrument.' What does 'blunt' mean in this context?

options.B: Physically heavy and difficult to carry.
options.D: Outdated and no longer in existence.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中『blunt instrument』是用來比喻 BMI 這種工具過於粗糙，無法精確診斷複雜的健康狀況，就像一把鈍刀無法進行精細手術一樣。選項 B 誤解了『blunt』在形容工具時的隱喻含義；選項 C 過度誇大了危險性；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章提到 BMI 目前仍被廣泛使用，並未消失。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the future of obesity diagnosis?

options.A: BMI should be banned immediately because it is completely useless for all medical purposes.
options.B: The medical community is shifting toward a more personalized approach that looks beyond simple weight-to-height ratios.
options.C: The new diagnostic system is perfect and will eliminate all errors in medical diagnosis.
options.D: Doctors should stop measuring weight entirely and focus only on organ health.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章的核心論點在於 BMI 雖然簡單好用，但因其不夠精確，醫學界正逐漸轉向結合更多生理指標（如器官功能、腰圍）的個人化診斷模式。選項 A 過於激進，文章並未主張全面禁用；選項 C 誇大了新系統的效能；選項 D 則是極端化了文章的建議，文章主張的是『結合』而非完全放棄舊有測量。
